\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{کھڑکھڑانا} (khaṛkhaṛānā)}{کھڑکھڑانا (khaṛkhaṛānā)}]{\ur{کھڑکھڑانا} (khaṛkhaṛānā) — to rattle}

\label{lesson:UR-C502-kharkharana}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to melt (something), then the Urdu for to plate (with metal).
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{کھڑکھڑانا}}
\textbf{\ur{کھڑکھڑانا}} — \emph{khaṛkhaṛānā} — \textquotedblleft{}to rattle\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{ہوا} \ur{میں} \ur{کھڑکی} \ur{کھڑکھڑاتی} \ur{ہے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{hawā meṅ khiṛkī khaṛkhaṛātī hai.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The window rattles in the wind.
\end{quote}

Past (it …): \ur{وہ} \ur{دروازہ} \ur{کھڑکھڑایا}, \emph{voh darvāzā khaṛkhaṛāyā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{کھڑکھڑانا}} (\emph{khaṛkhaṛānā}) is inherited from Sanskrit \emph{khaṭakhaṭāyatē}, \textquotedblleft{}crackles\textquotedblright{}, a word imitating the sound (CDIAL 3771).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{khaṛkhaṛānā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{khaṛkhaṛānā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{hawā meṅ khiṛkī khaṛkhaṛātī hai.} — The window rattles in the wind.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for to melt (something), then the Urdu for to plate (with metal), then say \emph{khaṛkhaṛānā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{کھڑکھڑانا} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To rattle\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{قبضہ} (qabzā)}{قبضہ (qabzā)}]{\ur{قبضہ} (qabzā) — a hinge; possession (a hold on something)}

\label{lesson:UR-C502-qabza}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to plate (with metal), then the Urdu for to rattle.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{قبضہ}}
\textbf{\ur{قبضہ}} — \emph{qabzā} — \textquotedblleft{}a hinge; possession (a hold on something)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{دروازے} \ur{کا} \ur{ایک} \ur{قبضہ} \ur{ٹوٹ} \ur{گیا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{darvāze kā ek qabzā ṭūṭ gayā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
One of the door's hinges has broken.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{قبضہ}} (\emph{qabzā}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{qabḍa}, \textquotedblleft{}a grip, a handle\textquotedblright{}; Urdu also uses it for \textquotedblleft{}possession\textquotedblright{}, a hold on something, while the sense \textquotedblleft{}a hinge\textquotedblright{} came later, and the sources we use do not show how it arose.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{qabzā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{qabzā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{darvāze kā ek qabzā ṭūṭ gayā.} — One of the door's hinges has broken.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for to plate (with metal), then the Urdu for to rattle, then say \emph{qabzā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{قبضہ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A hinge; possession (a hold on something)\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{نٹ} (naṭ)}{نٹ (naṭ)}]{\ur{نٹ} (naṭ) — a nut (for a bolt)}

\label{lesson:UR-C502-nat}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to rattle, then the Urdu for a hinge.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{نٹ}}
\textbf{\ur{نٹ}} — \emph{naṭ} — \textquotedblleft{}a nut (for a bolt)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{سائیکل} \ur{کا} \ur{ایک} \ur{نٹ} \ur{کھو} \ur{گیا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{sāikil kā ek naṭ kho gayā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
One of the bicycle's nuts has gone missing.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{نٹ}} (\emph{naṭ}) is borrowed from English \emph{nut}, the small metal piece on a bolt.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for to rattle, then the Urdu for a hinge, then say \emph{naṭ} again

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{زنگ} (zang)}{زنگ (zang)}]{\ur{زنگ} (zang) — rust}

\label{lesson:UR-C502-zang}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a hinge, then the Urdu for a nut (for a bolt).

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{اسپرنگ} (ispring)}{اسپرنگ (ispring)}]{\ur{اسپرنگ} (ispring) — a metal spring (a coil)}

\label{lesson:UR-C502-ispring}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a nut (for a bolt), then the Urdu for rust.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{اسپرنگ}}
\textbf{\ur{اسپرنگ}} — \emph{ispring} — \textquotedblleft{}a metal spring (a coil)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اس} \ur{پرانے} \ur{پلنگ} \ur{کے} \ur{اسپرنگ} \ur{کمزور} \ur{ہیں۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{is purāne palang ke ispring kamzor haiṅ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The springs of this old bed are weak.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{اسپرنگ}} (\emph{ispring}) is borrowed from English \emph{spring}, the coil of metal.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}
